title: CGU's ALICE robot flags overpricing in three 2024 Rio de Janeiro federal hospital tenders; one suspended, one revoked, one re-estimated
summary: CGU ALICE alerts: three 2024 federal hospital tenders in Rio de Janeiro state suspended, revoked or re-estimated; R$19.4m overpricing risk flagged (sum of three confirmed risks)
account: On 14 January 2025 the Controladoria-Geral da União (CGU) reported that ALICE (Analisador de Licitações, Contratos e Editais), its in-house tool that reads procurement documents with artificial-intelligence techniques and issues risk alerts, had flagged three 2024 tenders of federal hospitals in the state of Rio de Janeiro. At the Hospital Federal de Ipanema, tender 90016/2024 for laminated gowns (estimated R$16,726,635.12) was suspended after auditors confirmed an overpricing risk of R$10,925,029.92, and tender 90017/2024 for nursing supplies (estimated R$15,450,714.80), where an overpricing risk of R$5,994,645.60 was also found, was re-estimated at R$12,386,939.96, a saving of R$3,063,774.84. At the Hospital Federal dos Servidores do Estado, tender 90002/2024 (estimated R$26,578,591.02) was revoked after a confirmed risk of R$2,475,054.36. The release gives no total; the three confirmed risks sum to R$19,394,729.88, the R$19.4 million of the headline and metric. The release gives no dates for the suspension and revocation, so the statement date is used.
purpose: Continuous automated audit of federal procurement notices to detect risks such as inflated price estimates before contracts are awarded
system: ALICE (Analisador de Licitações, Contratos e Editais), CGU text-mining and AI alert tool
domain: Public administration: government audit and procurement control
segment: Federal internal control (anti-corruption and waste prevention)
taxonomy_note: Benefit type from Trustible's published framework (1 May 2024): Reduced Risk, stakeholder organizational, category Legal, 'Reduction in potential for harm, especially potential legal harm.' The CGU documents confirmed overpricing risk of R$19,394,729.88 across three tenders removed before award by suspension, revocation and re-estimate. Category 'harm prevented' because the overpriced tenders were in progress, the ALICE alert and audit intervened, and the CGU records the three outcomes as results of that action.

ratings.reason: No identifiable individual beneficiary is named; the beneficiaries are public bodies and, indirectly, taxpayers.

Material to the two hospitals and the federal budget: a documented R$3,063,774.84 reduction on one tender and removal of R$13.4 million of confirmed overpricing risk through one suspension and one revocation.
Small at national scale; three tenders among 118,069 processes analyzed in 2024.

ai_role.statement: The CGU release states that each tender 'teve alerta do Robô ALICE' and that auditors then confirmed the overpricing risk; the suspension, revocation and re-estimation are described as results of that audit action. Human auditors and hospital managers made the decisions; ALICE's role was detection and triage. Developer and deployer are the same public body, so this is the body documenting its own tool; the gov.br page was retrieved from the Internet Archive because the live page was restricted during Brazil's 2026 electoral period.

TCE-MG state-level use of Alice: in December 2022 TCE-MG published the result of an audit covering 2,297 state and municipal tenders in August 2022 alone, with corrections to notices worth R$91,723,011.31 (Atricon, 28 Jun 2023; publication month only)

revisions.change: Record drafted from the cited sources.
Paired with AI Incident Database incident 738 (medium confidence); severity not given by the source.

Extended the Licitação.net quote to the end of its sentence; added the R$5,994,645.60 risk on tender 90017/2024 and stated that the R$19.4 million headline figure is the registry's sum of the three confirmed risks (R$19,394,729.88) because the CGU gives no total; dated the Revista da CGU article 20 December 2022 and re-described it as a practitioner report (relato) in the CGU's own journal; moved the record to 'harm prevented' because the overpriced tenders were in progress and the CGU records their suspension, revocation and re-estimate as results of the alert-driven audit; set the benefit type to Trustible's 'Reduced Risk' from the published framework (entry quoted in the taxonomy note; data/taxonomy.json must carry it) so that the type names the benefit instead of a closest fit; noted that the road-works echo year is inferred from the 2024 year-end release and that December 2022 is when TCE-MG published its audit result; and located the hospitals in the state of Rio de Janeiro as the release does.
Benefit type kept within Trustible's six types (Improved Organizational Efficiency); the sweep's proposed 'Reduced Risk' is not in the taxonomy.
